items.title: AI Literacy for Higher Education: Responsible AI Use in Research, Thesis Writing, and Academic Reporting
items.abstract: The widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI (GenAI) tools, in higher education has created significant opportunities in research, thesis writing, and academic reporting processes, while also raising important questions regarding academic integrity, accuracy, ethical responsibility, and human oversight. To promote informed and responsible use of AI while benefiting from the opportunities it offers, this study presents a framework for the ethical, critical, and responsible use of AI in research, thesis writing, and academic reporting in higher education. AI literacy is conceptualized not merely as the ability to use AI tools, but as the competence to evaluate and verify AI-generated information, establish ethical boundaries, and maintain academic responsibility. The study is designed as a narrative literature review and thematic evaluation based on academic studies and policy and guidance documents published by international organizations. The literature is examined in the contexts of AI literacy, generative AI, research ethics, academic integrity, thesis writing, source verification, and academic reporting. The findings indicate that AI can be used as a supportive tool in academic processes; however, scientific evaluation, source verification, methodological decision-making, and ultimate academic responsibility should remain with humans. The study argues that responsible AI use in higher education should be grounded in the principles of human oversight, critical thinking, verification, transparency, data privacy, and academic integrity. Accordingly, AI literacy should be regarded not merely as a technological skill but as a fundamental component of future academic and research competencies in higher education. items.title: AI Revolution: The Death of Business Administration and the Birth of Inalienable Leadership
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly performing administrative, analytical, coordinating, monitoring, communication, and decision-support functions historically associated with managers and business administration. This transformation does not imply the disappearance of organizations, management, managers, or business schools. It marks the erosion of administration as an exclusively human domain and as the principal justification for managerial authority. When machines can analyze, plan, coordinate, evaluate, recommend, and execute, leadership must be grounded in something deeper than superior control of information and process. Existing leadership theories explain traits, skills, behaviors, relationships, ethics, adaptation, collective agency, technological mediation, and organizational effectiveness. The documented review nevertheless identifies a higher-order question that these traditions do not make their central organizing principle: who retains final authority and responsibility over purposes, institutions, and civilizational direction when machines increasingly participate in organizational and social decision-making? This conceptual, theoretical, normative, and integrative working paper introduces and timestamps Inalienable Leadership as the first metatheory of leadership specifically formulated for the age of artificial intelligence and robotics, advances it as the overarching metatheory of leadership in that age, and formally records it as the twelfth and culminating original contribution of the complete FILE contribution system. FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution remains the core management theory and diagnostic framework. Its place within the broader leadership architecture is expressed by the formula Leadership = Intelligence + Character + Judgment, with Intelligence conceptualized through FILE, Character through SQL, and Judgment through LENS. Inalienable Leadership integrates, grounds, governs, and gives civilizational direction to FILE and the complete FILE contribution system. The paper establishes a three-level hierarchy: Inalienable Leadership; the FILE Architecture (including the five meta-intelligences, the nested intelligences, and the Five Emergent Outcomes, which are products of the integrated exercise of FILE + SQL + LENS); and the first eleven original contributions and their associated structures. It preserves the specific roles of Human Irreducibility, HACK, HTTPS, LENS, MAIL, MLT, and RC while placing them under one civilizational principle: humanity may share work and intelligence with machines, but it cannot surrender its final authority and responsibility for the purposes, institutions, and direction of civilization. The future will not be determined by what machines can do, but by whether humanity remains capable of leading what it creates. Humans + Machines, under human leadership.

items.title: AI Use and Learning Outcomes Among Undergraduate Students: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation, Locus of Control, and Learning Preferences
items.abstract: Background. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has created new opportunities for personalized learning, although its contribution to student achievement remains theoretically and empirically contested. Purpose. This study examined the direct and indirect effects of AI use on conceptual understanding and problem-solving ability through learning motivation, locus of control, and learning preferences. Method. A quantitative explanatory design was employed with 88 pre-service teachers enrolled in an Instructional Media course at a teacher education institution in Central Java, Indonesia. Data were collected using validated questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Preliminary analyses were conducted using SPSS, while the measurement and structural models were evaluated through PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Novelty. This study simultaneously tested three psychological and learning-related mediators within a single structural model, thereby extending previous research that primarily examined the direct relationship between AI use and academic performance. Results. AI use significantly predicted learning motivation and locus of control but did not significantly influence learning preferences. Learning motivation significantly predicted learning outcomes and mediated the relationship between AI use and learning outcomes. In contrast, locus of control and learning preferences showed no significant mediating effects. The direct effect of AI use on learning outcomes was also nonsignificant. Conclusion. AI contributes to student learning primarily by strengthening learning motivation rather than through direct technological exposure. Effective AI integration should therefore emphasize reflective, autonomous, and cognitively engaging learning activities.

items.title: AI-Assisted Clinical Decision Support Versus Standard Teleconsultation in Adult Medicine: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy, Referral and Testing Decisions, and Clinician Confidence
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into teleconsultation, but its effects on clinician performance remain uncertain. We assessed whether clinician-facing AI improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces referrals or testing, and increases clinician confidence compared with standard teleconsultation or conventional resources. Methods: This retrospectively registered systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 and Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE, publisher-indexed platforms, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and backward and forward citation searches were performed from inception to 1 August 2026. Eligible studies evaluated clinician-facing AI in adult primary, urgent, or general medical teleconsultation or in high-fidelity virtual consultation designs and reported diagnostic, referral/testing, or confidence outcomes. One reviewer screened records, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias using the design-appropriate QUADAS-2, RoB 2, and ROBINS-I domains, with a second pass for consistency. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, the results were synthesized narratively. Results: Of 31 records identified, 25 remained after duplicate removal, 18 full texts were assessed, and six studies were included: two randomized virtual experiments, two retrospectives virtual care cohorts, one randomized crossover conversational AI study, and one provider-to-provider telemedicine case series. In a telehealth screening experiment, AI improved diagnostic prediction, but physicians given a large language model showed no significant benefit (adjusted difference, two percentage points; 95% CI, −4 to 8). Across 102,059 virtual encounters, an AI-generated differential included the clinician’s final diagnosis in 84.2%, although the reference was not independent. AI-assisted urgent care recommendations were rated optimal more often than final physician recommendations (77.1% vs. 67.1%). AI did not reduce unnecessary referrals; one experiment found more confirmatory testing requests and lower trust than with a familiar clinical score. Certainty was low or very low for the principal clinical outcomes. Conclusions: AI may support teleconsultation decisions, but evidence that it reduces unnecessary referrals or meaningfully increases clinician confidence is insufficient. Pragmatic trials using independent patient-level reference standards are needed. Registration: This completed review was retrospectively registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF); no protocol was published before study selection.

items.title: AI-Assisted Integration of Midgut Digestive Enzymes and Gut Microbiota in Samia ricini: A Predictive Framework for Sustainable Eri-Silk Production
items.abstract: Abstract The eri silkworm, Samia ricini (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae), is an economically important polyphagous silk-producing insect whose productivity is influenced by host-plant quality, digestive physiology, larval development and associated gut microorganisms. The midgut represents a major interface between dietary nutrients and physiological utilization, while the resident microbial community may contribute to nutrient transformation and host adaptation. Although previous studies have independently investigated digestive enzymes, host-plant effects and gut microbial diversity in S. ricini, an integrated predictive framework combining biochemical, microbiome and production variables remains comparatively underdeveloped. The present study proposes an AI-assisted framework for integrating midgut digestive enzyme activity, gut microbiota and larval/cocoon traits in S. ricini. Three host-plant diets—Ricinus communis, Ailanthus altissima and Manihot esculenta—are considered within the proposed experimental framework. Digestive activities of α-amylase, protease, lipase and cellulase are proposed to be evaluated together with 16S rRNA-based bacterial community profiling. Larval growth, survival, cocoon weight, shell weight and shell percentage are incorporated as production-related variables. Statistical approaches including ANOVA, correlation analysis, diversity analysis and PERMANOVA are combined with machine-learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost and Support Vector Regression. For methodological demonstration, a simulated dataset was constructed using biologically plausible ranges rather than experimental observations. The simulated analysis illustrates how integrated biochemical and microbial variables can be used to predict larval and cocoon performance and how SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence can identify influential predictors. The framework suggests that microbiome–enzyme interactions may provide useful candidate biomarkers for future validation. However, simulated findings should not be interpreted as empirical evidence. The proposed framework provides a basis for future experimental studies aimed at microbiome-informed feeding, precision rearing and sustainable eri-silk production.

items.title: AI-Driven Development of Smart Chemical Sensors for Rapid Detection of Environmental Pollution
items.abstract: Abstract Environmental pollution is a complex and continuously evolving problem that requires rapid, sensitive and decentralized analytical technologies. Conventional analytical techniques such as atomic absorption spectrometry, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, gas chromatography and high-performance liquid chromatography provide high analytical performance but generally require sophisticated instrumentation, laboratory infrastructure, sample preparation and trained personnel. Smart chemical sensors offer an attractive alternative because they can provide rapid measurements with portable and potentially low-cost instrumentation. However, environmental samples contain multiple interfering species, and sensor responses may be nonlinear, unstable or affected by temperature, pH, humidity and sensor ageing. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), provides new opportunities to overcome these limitations by extracting complex patterns from chemical-sensor responses and converting them into qualitative or quantitative information. This paper reviews the development of AI-driven smart chemical sensors for rapid environmental pollution detection, with emphasis on electrochemical sensors, gas-sensor arrays, optical sensors and nanomaterial-based sensing platforms. The application of machine-learning approaches including principal component analysis, support-vector machines, artificial neural networks, random forests and deep-learning models for signal processing, classification, quantification and sensor-drift compensation is discussed. Recent studies demonstrate the integration of deep learning, electrochemical sensing and Internet-of-Things technology for simultaneous detection of heavy metals in water. The paper also proposes an integrated framework combining chemical recognition, signal transduction, AI-based data interpretation, wireless communication and environmental decision support. Major challenges, including limited datasets, matrix effects, sensor drift, model interpretability and field validation, are discussed. AI-enabled chemical sensors have considerable potential to transform environmental monitoring from periodic laboratory analysis toward rapid, portable and intelligent pollution surveillance.

items.title: AI-Driven Green Chemistry for Sustainable Development: A Comprehensive Review Towards Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract The escalating global demand for chemicals, materials, and energy has intensified concerns regarding resource depletion, hazardous waste generation, energy consumption, and environmental pollution. Green chemistry provides a sustainable paradigm by minimizing waste, reducing hazardous substances, improving energy efficiency, and promoting renewable resources. However, developing greener chemical processes traditionally requires extensive experimentation and optimization. Artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning, and predictive modeling—offers transformative opportunities to accelerate this transition. AI enables reaction prediction and optimization, catalyst discovery, green solvent selection, sustainable material design, toxicity prediction, waste minimization, and environmental monitoring by analyzing large chemical datasets and identifying relationships recognized through conventional approaches. Integration of AI with automation and advanced analytical techniques further enables faster, more efficient chemical research. This review discusses major applications of AI in green chemistry, emphasizing sustainable synthesis, catalysis, solvents, materials, waste management, energy technologies, and analytical chemistry. We address challenges associated with data quality, model interpretability, experimental validation, computational energy consumption, and industrial scale-up. items.title: AI-Driven Precision Agriculture and Crop Resilience: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Remote Sensing for Climate-Resilient Indian Agriculture: A Vision for Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Agriculture is central to India's economic development, food security, rural employment, and the achievement of the Viksit Bharat@2047 vision. However, Indian agriculture faces increasingly complex challenges, including climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, pest and disease outbreaks, fragmented landholdings, market uncertainty, and unequal access to agricultural knowledge. These challenges require a transition from conventional, input-intensive agriculture towards data-driven, resource-efficient, climate-resilient and farmer-centric production systems. Agriculture in India is increasingly affected by climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, pest and disease outbreaks, and unpredictable weather conditions. These challenges threaten crop productivity and food security, particularly among small and marginal farmers. Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, and machine learning offer new opportunities to transform conventional agricultural practices into data-driven precision agriculture systems. This paper presents a conceptual framework for AI-driven precision agriculture aimed at improving crop resilience under changing climatic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI), combined with precision agriculture, Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, satellite imagery, drones, machine learning, robotics and digital public infrastructure, offers significant opportunities to transform Indian agriculture. AI can support crop and yield prediction, disease and pest identification, weather-based advisories, irrigation optimisation, soil management, crop insurance, market intelligence and early-warning systems. The paper also discusses challenges related to digital inclusion, data governance, affordability, AI reliability, farmer skills, privacy and institutional coordination. It argues that India's objective should not simply be the digitisation of agriculture, but the creation of an intelligent, inclusive and resilient agricultural ecosystem in which technology augments farmer knowledge and decision-making. By 2047, India can aspire to establish globally competitive agriculture that produces more with fewer resources, withstands climate shocks, generates higher and more stable farm incomes, and ensures sustainable food and nutritional security.

items.title: AI-Driven Smart Materials for Sustainable Energy Applications: Advancing Smart Technologies for Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced materials are increasingly being integrated to accelerate research in sustainable energy technologies. The paper presents a physics-based approach to AI-driven smart materials, focusing on photovoltaic conversion, batteries, supercapacitors, thermoelectric systems, and hydrogen technologies. It emphasizes that AI should support material screening and optimisation rather than replace fundamental physics. Materials such as perovskites, nanostructures, two-dimensional materials, electrode materials, and thermoelectric compounds are discussed. Analytical models are used to understand photovoltaic efficiency, capacitor energy, and thermoelectric performance. The study also proposes physics-informed machine learning to improve material prediction and optimisation. Key challenges include data quality, uncertainty, interpretability, extrapolation, and experimental validation. Overall, the AI–Physics–Experiment approach can accelerate materials research and contribute to sustainable energy development in India.

items.title: AI-Driven Systemic Risk in FinTech and an Integrated Framework for Risk Measurement, Audit, and Governance
items.abstract: This chapter examines the impact of artificial intelligence adoption on systemic risk in fintech-driven financial systems, emphasizing the need for integrated risk management, audit, and governance frameworks. The study develops a composite AI Risk Index using Principal Component Analysis to capture interactions between financial vulnerability, technological adoption, and institutional quality across 39 countries from 2010 to 2024 . Using fixed effects and dynamic panel GMM models alongside machine learning techniques, including Random Forest and SHAP explainability, the analysis identifies non-linear and threshold effects in the relationship between AI adoption and systemic risk. The findings show that AI can amplify systemic vulnerabilities beyond critical adoption levels, particularly in weak governance environments. The chapter also proposes a Risk–Audit–Governance framework and a risk zoning model, highlighting the importance of adaptive regulation, continuous auditing, and strong institutional capacity to ensure financial stability and accountability.

items.title: AI-Driven Workplace Surveillance and Employee Privacy: A Labour Law Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the modern workplace. Employers are increasingly using AI-enabled technologies to monitor attendance, productivity, communication, location, performance, behaviour and emotional responses of employees. While such technologies can offer advantages in terms of organisational efficiency, prevention of misconduct and management of large workforces, they also raise serious concerns over employee privacy, autonomy, dignity and labour rights. Traditional workplace monitoring was generally limited to physical observation, attendance registers and conventional electronic monitoring. AI has enabled wider collection of employee data, which is subsequently evaluated using automated systems. This research explores the relationship between AI-driven workplace surveillance and employee privacy rights, with reference to the Indian legal framework. It examines the challenges created by continuous monitoring, algorithmic decision-making, biometric surveillance, productivity tracking and employee profiling. The study argues that workplace surveillance should not be viewed solely as a question of managerial authority but should be addressed as a labour-rights and fundamental-rights issue. A balanced regulatory approach is therefore crucial to ensure that legitimate business interests do not override employee privacy and dignity. The research concludes with recommendations for transparency, proportionality, informed notice, data minimisation, human oversight and effective grievance mechanisms.

items.title: AI-enabled and comparator digital interventions for adolescent mental health (2020–2025): early detection, human–AI collaboration, and ethical governance—a PRISMA-ScR scoping review
items.abstract: Introduction Mental health difficulties among adolescents and youth (ages 10–24) are increasing globally, yet early intervention remains impeded by stigma, service shortages, and cultural barriers. AI-enabled technologies including chatbots, automated screening tools, and machine learning-based predictive models have been proposed as scalable approaches to address these gaps, alongside non-AI digital interventions such as therapist-guided internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) and smartphone-based CBT applications, which are examined as comparator evidence given their stronger controlled-design evidence base. Methods This scoping review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) reporting guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. A systematic database search across six databases (PubMed, Scopus, ProQuest, SpringerLink, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect), supplemented by manual and forward-citation searching, yielded 10,962 records, of which 19 studies met the predefined inclusion criteria. A Human-AI Collaboration Role framework comprising a four-level continuum from fully human-led to fully automated delivery was applied as a predefined coding dimension across all included studies. Results Most studies focused on depression and anxiety among mid-to-late adolescents in high-income countries (68.4%). Therapist-guided iCBT was the most rigorously studied format using randomized and controlled designs; AI chatbots, predictive models, and large language model (LLM)-based systems demonstrated feasibility or engagement outcomes in a limited number of studies and contexts, though randomized diagnostic chatbot trials specifically remain absent for participants under 18 years; at least one randomized non-diagnostic chatbot trial (a body-image intervention) has been conducted in this age group. Equity-related reporting was inconsistent: socioeconomic status was reported in only 10.5% of studies and cultural adaptation in 42.1%; restriction to English-language publications may further underrepresent non-Western and low- and middle-income-country evidence relevant to these equity findings. Key implementation challenges included inconsistent safeguarding protocols for minors, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and insufficient integration with clinical and educational systems. Discussion The evidence base remains preliminary and methodologically heterogeneous, insufficient to support conclusions about clinical effectiveness or generalizability to diverse adolescent populations. These findings represent a descriptive map of the current evidence landscape rather than an assessment of effectiveness. Future research should prioritize adequately powered adolescent-focused trials, participatory co-design approaches, culturally informed adaptations, and transparent ethical governance frameworks to ensure responsible development of AI-enabled digital mental health tools for youth. Because the included studies were heterogeneous and no formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken, this review does not establish comparative clinical effectiveness, safety, or superiority of AI-enabled interventions. Systematic Review Registration https://osf.io/sbpk2 , doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/SBPK2 .

items.title: AI-Enhanced Performance Appraisal Systems: Assessing the Interplay Between Machine Feedback, Employee Motivation, and Career Mobility
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into performance appraisal systems has fundamentally transformed how organizations evaluate, reward, and guide talent. This paper examines the complex interplay between automated machine feedback, employee intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, and long-term career mobility within modern corporate structures. Traditional performance reviews, historically plagued by manager bias, infrequent feedback cycles, and administrative lag, are increasingly being replaced by real-time, algorithmic evaluation tools that continuously monitor productivity, communication patterns, and milestone attainment. While these advanced systems offer unprecedented objectivity, data granularity, and operational efficiency, they simultaneously introduce critical psychological and structural challenges for the workforce. The research investigates how algorithmic oversight impacts employee motivation, exploring the fine line between constructive data-driven guidance and dehumanizing surveillance. When machine feedback is perceived as opaque, overly punitive, or devoid of contextual empathy, it can trigger algorithmic anxiety, disengagement, and strategic gaming of metrics. Conversely, when integrated transparently, AI-driven insights can empower employees with actionable developmental pathways, aligning daily performance with overarching career trajectories. The study further analyzes the implications of automated career mobility, evaluating how machine-generated talent mapping influences promotions, skill-gap identification, and succession planning. It highlights the risk of algorithmic bias reinforcing historical inequities, thereby restricting advancement opportunities for diverse employee segments if human oversight is absent. Methodologically, this paper synthesizes contemporary organizational psychology literature with a comparative evaluation of organizations deploying AI-augmented human resource management systems. The analytical framework correlates the frequency and framing of machine feedback with metrics of employee retention, morale, and promotional velocity. The findings suggest that optimal performance outcomes are achieved not through pure automation, but through a hybrid model where AI serves as an objective diagnostic tool that amplifies—rather than replaces—human managerial mentorship and empathy. Ultimately, this study provides human resource leaders and technologists with a strategic framework for designing ethical, motivation-enhancing appraisal architectures that foster sustainable career growth and organizational agility.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Performance Appraisal Systems: Assessing the Interplay Between Machine Feedback, Employee Motivation, and Career Mobility
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into performance appraisal systems has fundamentally transformed how organizations evaluate, reward, and guide talent. This paper examines the complex interplay between automated machine feedback, employee intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, and long-term career mobility within modern corporate structures. Traditional performance reviews, historically plagued by manager bias, infrequent feedback cycles, and administrative lag, are increasingly being replaced by real-time, algorithmic evaluation tools that continuously monitor productivity, communication patterns, and milestone attainment. While these advanced systems offer unprecedented objectivity, data granularity, and operational efficiency, they simultaneously introduce critical psychological and structural challenges for the workforce. The research investigates how algorithmic oversight impacts employee motivation, exploring the fine line between constructive data-driven guidance and dehumanizing surveillance. When machine feedback is perceived as opaque, overly punitive, or devoid of contextual empathy, it can trigger algorithmic anxiety, disengagement, and strategic gaming of metrics. Conversely, when integrated transparently, AI-driven insights can empower employees with actionable developmental pathways, aligning daily performance with overarching career trajectories. The study further analyzes the implications of automated career mobility, evaluating how machine-generated talent mapping influences promotions, skill-gap identification, and succession planning. It highlights the risk of algorithmic bias reinforcing historical inequities, thereby restricting advancement opportunities for diverse employee segments if human oversight is absent. Methodologically, this paper synthesizes contemporary organizational psychology literature with a comparative evaluation of organizations deploying AI-augmented human resource management systems. The analytical framework correlates the frequency and framing of machine feedback with metrics of employee retention, morale, and promotional velocity. The findings suggest that optimal performance outcomes are achieved not through pure automation, but through a hybrid model where AI serves as an objective diagnostic tool that amplifies—rather than replaces—human managerial mentorship and empathy. Ultimately, this study provides human resource leaders and technologists with a strategic framework for designing ethical, motivation-enhancing appraisal architectures that foster sustainable career growth and organizational agility.

items.title: AI-Generated Content, Authenticity, and Corporate Responsibility in the Digital Economy
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has transformed visual art, raising questions about authenticity, creativity, and authorship. This chapter examines how authenticity is redefined in AI-generated imagery by integrating perspectives from aesthetics, creativity studies, and AI research. It proposes a process-oriented framework in which authenticity is understood as a relational and context-dependent construct emerging from interactions between human creators, algorithms, and audiences. Generative AI challenges traditional notions of originality by introducing distributed creative agency, while lacking intentionality behind its outputs. Human–AI collaboration shifts artistic practice from manual execution to conceptual direction, curation, and interpretation. Audience perceptions of authenticity are shaped not only by visual quality but also by knowledge of production processes. The chapter argues that authenticity is not diminished but transformed, requiring new frameworks and stronger emphasis on transparency, trust, and responsible governance.

items.title: AI-Generated Review Summaries And Consumer Purchase Decisions: A Conceptual Framework For Indian Gen Z Consumers
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is changing how consumers search for, evaluate and use information in digital marketplaces. One emerging application is the use of AI-generated review summaries, which condense large volumes of online consumer reviews into concise statements about product strengths, weaknesses and frequently mentioned attributes. Such summaries can reduce information overload and improve search efficiency, but they also raise concerns regarding credibility, transparency, objectivity, selective omission and consumer reliance on machine-generated interpretations of peer opinions. This study examines AI-generated review summaries and their potential influence on purchase decisions among Indian Gen Z consumers. The study is primarily secondary-research-led and synthesises recent literature on AI-mediated electronic word-of-mouth, review credibility, transparency, trust and perceived diagnosticity. To complement the secondary evidence, an exploratory primary survey of 120 respondents collected through Google Forms is incorporated as an empirical component. The study adopts the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) perspective and signalling theory to structure the relationships among perceived transparency, perceived usefulness, perceived objectivity, consumer trust, perceived diagnosticity and purchase intention. The paper proposes that trust and diagnosticity function as important mechanisms through which characteristics of AI-generated review summaries can influence purchase intention. The empirical component is designed to provide descriptive and exploratory evidence rather than to replace the broader secondary research base. Statistical analysis includes respondent profiling, descriptive statistics, reliability assessment, correlation analysis and appropriate hypothesis testing, subject to the structure of the 120-response dataset. The study contributes to understanding how AI-mediated review information can support consumer decision-making while highlighting the importance of transparency, balanced representation and access to original reviews.

items.abstract: Abstract India's transition toward a renewable energy-led economy faces critical challenges in grid stability, demand forecasting, and efficient integration of intermittent power sources such as solar and wind. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to overcoming these constraints, enabling predictive load forecasting, real-time fault detection, and autonomous demand-response management across smart grid. Grid Mission, the IndiaAI Mission, and NITI Aayog's National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence. It further examines barriers to scale, including high implementation costs, inconsistent data interoperability across state utilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities in AI-integrated grid systems, and the skills gap in AI-energy hybrid expertise. Through a review-based analytical framework, the paper proposes an integrated model aligning AI-enabled smart grid deployment with SDG-7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG-13 (Climate Action) within India's Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The findings suggest that AI-optimized energy systems, if scaled with supportive policy and skilled workforce development, can position India as a global leader in sustainable, technology-driven energy infrastructure.

items.title: AI-Powered Personalized Learning: Enhancing Student Academic Achievement and Motivation
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) applications have driven education toward more adaptive and personalized learning experiences and environments. By offering educators tools to customize learning paths, adapt resources to students’ needs, and provide tailored feedback, AI applications are able to boost student academic achievement and motivation. This study seeks to assess the impact of an AI-enhanced learning approach on students’ academic achievement and motivation. We employed a quasi-experimental method for this study with a total of 54 sixth-grade pupils at a private bilingual school in Barka, Oman split into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group was taught using AI applications and the control group was taught using the Moodle learning management system. Results of the study indicate that the AI-powered approach significantly increased students’ academic achievement (p < .05) and motivation (p < .01), with notable gains in attention, confidence, and relevance. ’The findings of the study highlight the significant potential of AI to reshape learners’ experiences and enhance learning and motivation by providing adaptive and personalized learning. Given the small sample size and study environment, the generalizability of the results is limited. Future studies should investigate the scalability of AI-powered learning aids across different educational environments.

items.title: AIfred: Augmented Learning through Functional Robotic Embodiment at the Desk
items.abstract: Desk-based learning and creative activities benefit from handwritten engagement. However, current generative AI tools deliver guidance through a separate screen, creating a gap between where users think and where assistance appears. To address this, in this work we design AIfred, a desk-based robotic arm with a projector mounted at the end-effector that places AI-generated guidance alongside handwritten work. AIfred combines workspace perception, context-aware content generation, and robot-mediated projection to support math assignments, image generation, and drawing tasks. In a user study (n = 36), we compared AIfred against ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Luna) running on a laptop. Both tools performed comparably while assistance was available during the math assignment (6.7 vs. 7.3/10, p = .41), but AIfred improved short-term learning transfer by 60% once assistance was withdrawn (7.0 vs. 4.4/10, p = .003). In addition, independent art and design professors ranked drawings produced with AIfred better in 33 of 36 cases. Our findings indicate that spatially co-located AI assistance benefits tasks whose guidance shares a spatial frame with the work.

items.title: AIMS: An Agentic AI Framework for Sim-to-Real Multi-Modal ISAC
items.abstract: Multi-modal integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables environmental perception and reliable connectivity for intelligent wireless networks. Data-driven multi-modal ISAC models depend heavily on annotated real-world data to learn relationships across sensing and wireless observations, thereby constraining scalable deployment. Although synthetic data generation reduces the burden, adapting existing simulation pipelines to a target deployment requires consistent scene, sensing, wireless, and learning configurations, while mismatches among these coupled components impair sim-to-real transferability. To address the challenge, we propose an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for sim-to-real multi-modal ISAC, named AIMS. Given a natural-language deployment request specifying the target task, deployment conditions, and real-data budget, AIMS derives a deployment-specific sim-to-real configuration and coordinates its execution to produce a deployment-specific task model. A two-agent architecture coordinates scene construction with task learning. A scene construction agent generates geographically grounded, synchronized sensing and wireless records from shared physical states, while a scene understanding agent configures task-relevant modalities and mixture-of-experts (MoE) learning for zero-shot inference or few-shot adaptation. Structured domain knowledge guides dependency-aware planning, while validation evidence supports feedback-driven revision of affected decisions. Experiments on the real-world DeepSense 6G dataset demonstrate improved vehicle detection and beam prediction over the considered simulation and fusion baselines. A separate orchestration benchmark evaluates task interpretation, dependency reasoning, and feedback-driven replanning across diverse deployment requests, showing improved plan correctness with structured domain knowledge and validation feedback.

items.title: AIR-LLM: Broadcasting AI Weights over Radio for Memory-Free Edge LLM Inference via RF Computing
items.abstract: Next-generation large language models (LLMs) are expanding from the cloud to ubiquitous edge devices. However, edge devices typically either lack the memory to store increasingly large LLM weights or, even with enough memory, spend unaffordable energy on loading the weights. This raises our question: can an edge device run an LLM without storing or loading its weights, but receive them over the air and consume them on the fly? Inspired by wireless broadcasting, we present AIR-LLM, an LLM inference architecture for edge devices, which is composed of: (i) a central radio (e.g., 5G base stations) that broadcasts the LLM weights into the air, and (ii) the edge user that receives the weights and completes the general matrix-vector multiplication (GEMV) of LLM inference directly in the radio frequency (RF) domain using RF mixers. To further shorten the airtime, AIR-LLM exploits MIMO spatial multiplexing and proposes an energy-efficient precoder-postcoder pair on the edge to calibrate its own wireless channel. Since the central radio stays user-unaware, AIR-LLM is user-scalable so that one broadcast serves unlimited users within its coverage. We implement AIR-LLM on the NVIDIA Sionna ray-traced channels of two real-world urban scenes and the profiling of a real RF mixer. With a WikiText-2 perplexity degradation of 4.0% on LLaMA-3.1-8B, AIR-LLM saves the energy by 157.7x/40.4x against the FP16 and weight-only quantization baselines; with 20 users, its airtime is 104.1x/26.0x shorter, respectively.

items.title: Algorithmic Oversight: Caremark's Fiduciary Framework Applied to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence now drives core corporate decision, such as loan approvals and hiring screens, yet corporate boards have largely treated its governance as a management-level policy questions rather than a fiduciary obligation. This paper argues that this framing is mistaken, using Delaware's Caremark doctrine, as refined by Marchand v. Barnhill, In re Boeing, and In re McDonald's. The relevant cases already impose an enforceable duty on boards to actively oversee mission algorithmic systems, and by applying Marchand's mission-critical standard, this paper demonstrates that AI performs core business functions that expose companies to anti-discrimination, consumer protection, and securities liability. The paper also identifies a structural problem that existing doctrine has not confronted: unlike the legible red flags at issue in Caremark, Boeing, and Clovis Oncology, AI systems generate outputs without human-readable explanations, allowing boards to receive clean compliance reports from systems that are producing unlawful outcomes. This "black box problem" requires reestablishing what good-faith oversight demands and when the underlying risk bypasses traditional reporting structures. Drawing on In re SolarWinds and the officer liability extension in McDonald's, this paper proposes a scalable framework for reasonable AI oversight, including board-level AI audit committees, a Chief AI Officer role with reporting duties to the General Counsel and CEO, mandatory governance disclosure, and a safe harbor for compliance. Ultimately, this paper challenges that the doctrinal tools to govern AI already exist within Delaware law, and all that remains is for boards to act before litigation forces the question.

items.title: Algorithmically Alone
items.abstract: Platform economies are reorganising the everyday conditions through which urban residents feel connected, isolated, or at home. Discussions of gig work typically begin with flexibility and income, overlooking how apps, ratings, incentives, and algorithmic decisions reshape the social setting of work itself. This chapter argues that urban loneliness should be understood not only as a private feeling but as an outcome shaped by how work, time, and urban space are organised. Drawing on social capital theory, economic sociology, urban studies, and research on algorithmic management, the chapter develops a conceptual framework explaining how platform design weakens some forms of social connection while enabling new forms of worker solidarity. The discussion considers how these dynamics intersect with gender, psychological strain, and migrant status. Cases from Uber, Ola, Urban Company, Indian delivery platforms, New York City, Seattle, the European Union, and India's social-security framework illustrate these dynamics in practice.

items.title: Alignment of bricolage practice: How supply chain managers mitigate risks through human–AI teaming
items.abstract: Background As organizations embed algorithmic agents in operations, alignment is presumed to make human–AI teams safer and more effective. Yet it leaves the orientation of alignment unexamined, that is, what humans and agents actually coordinate around. Objective Drawing on bricolage theory, this study distinguishes three orientations of alignment: tangible-resource, opportunity-oriented, and risk-oriented, then examines how each relates to collaborative fluency and to financial and inventory risk. Methods We analyzed 141 simulated supply-chain teams, each pairing a human manager with seven rule-based AI agents between 24 and 47 cycles. Behavioral logs were coded for alignment orientation, while collaborative fluency, risk behavior and outcomes were computed from logs by hierarchical regression. Results Tangible-resource alignment was associated with lower inventory redundancy and smaller drawdown. Risk-oriented alignment was associated with greater net-asset volatility and drawdown, associations that weakened once financing was controlled. Opportunity-oriented alignment showed no associations. No orientation explained collaborative fluency, and financing dominated financial risk. Conclusions Whether human–AI alignment reduces risk depends on its orientation. Tangible-resource alignment can buffer operational risk, but risk-oriented alignment may mark risk-taking rather than control it. Effective teaming depends less on more alignment than on aligning in right domain, with restraint in financing as the primary safeguard.

items.title: An End-to-End Workflow for Building Longitudinal Policy Measures From Government Web Sources Using Historical Reconstruction and LLM-Based Extraction
items.abstract: Background: Longitudinal policy research requires measures of what policy applied, when, and with what provisions, yet government sources are organized and preserved in ways that can make historical policy difficult to reconstruct. This study developed and evaluated an end-to-end workflow for constructing longitudinal policy measures from government web sources.Methods: The workflow was applied to NHS England’s Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS), a national policy specifying which primary-care workforce categories are eligible for reimbursement, from 2019/20 to 2026/27. It combined historical document recovery, variable specification, automated extraction against a human-coded reference standard, and longitudinal measure construction. Keyword, deterministic, and large language model (LLM) methods were compared across eight development and six later evaluation versions. Three simplified measurement strategies were compared with the author-verified longitudinal reference. Exploratory source recovery assessments were also conducted in Spain, France, and Australia.Results: Historical reconstruction identified 14 substantive document versions across eight policy years, including within-year changes in reimbursement eligibility, amounts, and conditions. Reimbursable primary-care workforce categories increased from 5 to 27, while the current NHS England landing page provided access to documents from only one policy year. On the six later evaluation versions, the LLM matched all scored reference-standard targets for eligibility status, effective dates, and reimbursement amounts, although eligibility conditions remained more difficult to extract. Simplified measurement strategies changed the reconstructed policy history. Using only the current specification could not recover historical eligibility, one specification per policy year assigned 96 eligible category-months (7.3%) too early, and keyword coding produced 138 category-month errors (10.5%).Conclusion: Valid longitudinal policy measurement requires historical reconstruction, explicit variable and dating rules, evaluation on later documents, and human verification. For health-politics research, this approach can support measures of changing governmental choices about eligibility, financing, conditions, and timing while distinguishing formal policy from implementation and outcomes.

items.title: An Idea to Explore: AI ‐Supported Digital Twin Laboratory for Risk‐Reduced and Immersive Biochemistry Education
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biochemistry education faces persistent challenges in equipping students with the skills required to manage complex laboratory protocols, advanced instrumentation, and analytical procedures, particularly in high‐risk or resource‐intensive experimental settings. Traditional hands‐on training is constrained by limited access to equipment, safety concerns, and high operational costs, hindering institutions from providing realistic and scalable laboratory experiences. However, Digital Twin technology presents a transformative alternative. It creates simulations of real biochemical laboratories, providing immersive, scalable, and cost‐efficient environments unconstrained by physical limitations. This approach supports interactive, avatar‐mediated engagement that bridges conceptual knowledge with applied practice. In this study, we aimed to introduce BioDTLab, a custom Digital Twin framework for biochemistry education that integrates Virtual Reality, Internet of Things, robotics, data analytics, and an Artificial Intelligence (AI)‐driven Virtual Chat‐GPT Tutor. BioDTLab synchronizes physical and digital domains to provide high‐fidelity simulations of biochemical processes and instrumentation, while the AI‐driven Virtual Chat‐GPT Tutor evaluates student engagement, comprehension, and procedural accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that Digital Twin frameworks, such as BioDTLab, can redefine biochemistry education by making advanced experiential learning more accessible, safe, and scalable, while reducing reliance on costly physical resources. BioDTLab integrates immersive simulation, real‐time data synchronization, and AI‐driven feedback to provide a sustainable model for future science education that enhances conceptual understanding and practical competence. In addition, its adaptability makes it suitable for instructional models, such as the flipped classroom, where pre‐laboratory virtual practice can complement and enhance in‐person laboratory training.

items.title: An Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (Icepms) A Single-Window Digital Ecosystem for Research & Development in Higher Education Institutions in India
items.abstract: Abstract India's higher education system has never lacked policy mandates for community engagement. What it has consistently lacked is a working mechanism to connect community-identified problems with academic institutions positioned to address them. This paper proposes the Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (ICEPMS) — a single-window digital ecosystem that bridges this gap by linking community demand directly to higher education delivery. The paper develops a five-stakeholder conceptual model through systematic analysis of national policy documents, international frameworks, and established scholarship on community-based participatory research (CBPR) and service-learning. The proposed system enables citizens, Gram Panchayat members, NGOs, and journalists to report local problems digitally; allows administrators to convert those problems into credit-mapped academic topics; enables colleges and students to execute Community Engagement Projects; records performance transparently; and facilitates funding from CSR departments and government officers based on verifiable institutional performance. The paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence as a supportive accelerator within the system. ICEPMS aligns with the mandates of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the UGC Guidelines for Fostering Social Responsibility and Community Engagement in Higher Education Institutions in India 2.0 (2022), and institutional Community Engagement Project frameworks. By providing operational infrastructure for existing policy intent, the paper contributes a practical framework for community engagement in Indian higher education.

items.abstract: An Integrated Computer Vision and Machine Learning Framework for Sorghum Disease Severity Assessment and Yield Prediction presents a technology-driven approach for automated crop health monitoring and yield estimation in sorghum cultivation. The study integrates computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms to identify and quantify disease severity from crop images and to predict potential yield based on relevant visual and agronomic characteristics. The framework aims to reduce the limitations of conventional manual disease assessment, which can be time-consuming and subject to human variability. Image processing and feature extraction techniques are employed to capture disease-related characteristics, while machine learning models support classification, severity estimation, and yield prediction. By combining disease assessment with yield forecasting, the proposed framework provides a comprehensive approach to precision agriculture and data-driven crop management. The work demonstrates the potential of artificial intelligence and computer vision to support timely decision-making, improve crop monitoring, and contribute to sustainable and efficient sorghum production.

items.title: An IoT-enabled multimodal AI system for classifying adolescent mental states using facial, motion, and postural data
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and evaluation of a human-centric smart mental environment that integrates internet of things (IoT)-enabled sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) for the early detection of adolescent mental health indicators. Adolescent mental health disorders, including stress, anxiety, and depression, are increasingly prevalent yet remain underdiagnosed due to reliance on subjective self-reports and clinical interviews. Early detection is critical but hindered by symptom underreporting and the absence of continuous, objective monitoring tools suitable for real-world environments. To address this gap, the proposed system captures three complementary modalities: (1) facial expression features using a front-facing camera, (2) body motion and acceleration patterns using a wearable accelerometer and gyroscope, and (3) postural pressure distribution using an eight-element pressure array positioned along the thoracic and lumbar regions. Multimodal data are preprocessed using temporal-spatial filtering, followed by a cross-modal attention-based fusion mechanism that dynamically weights the most informative modality within each time window. A supervised learning classifier then predicts four mental states: normal, stress, anxiety, and depression. The system was evaluated using a dataset collected from 64 adolescents aged 14–18 under semi-natural, classroom-like conditions. The proposed attention-based multimodal framework achieved an overall classification accuracy of 89.2%, significantly outperforming unimodal baselines (facial-only: 77.8%, motion-only: 74.5%, posture-only: 71.3%) and simple concatenation fusion (83.5%). The attention mechanism improved the classification F1-score to 0.88 and demonstrated robustness under lighting and posture variations. Statistical analysis confirmed the superiority of the multimodal approach (p < 0.01). The system provides a non-invasive, scalable, and human-centric solution for continuous adolescent mental health monitoring, with strong potential for deployment in schools and community health programs.

items.title: Anal Dysplasia: From Pathogenesis to Risk-based Screening and Management
items.abstract: Anal dysplasia is the precursor of most anal squamous cell carcinomas and represents the central target of contemporary anal cancer prevention. Increasing recognition of high-risk populations, together with a better understanding of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated carcinogenesis and the results of the Anal Cancer/HSIL Outcomes Research (ANCHOR) trial, has shifted the focus from detecting disease to preventing cancer through the identification and treatment of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL). This chapter reviews the current concepts underlying anal dysplasia, including its epidemiology, natural history, risk factors, pathogenesis, histopathologic classification, diagnostic evaluation, and available therapeutic strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on the transition from the traditional anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) classification to the Lower Anogenital Squamous Terminology (LAST) system, the pivotal role of high-resolution anoscopy with directed biopsy as the diagnostic reference standard, and the evidence supporting contemporary screening and treatment algorithms. Prevention is discussed as a continuum encompassing HPV vaccination, sexual health interventions, HIV prevention and treatment, early detection of HSIL, and long-term surveillance after therapy. Finally, the chapter highlights current challenges, including the need for standardized HRA training, development of centers of excellence, and international collaborative research to improve implementation, validate emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and precision risk prediction, and ultimately expand access to effective anal cancer prevention worldwide.

items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of construction projects, particularly roof rehabilitation work, which carries a high risk of accidents. This study aims to identify hazards, analyze risk levels, and determine risk controls for the Kepulungan Community Health Center Roof Rehabilitation Project using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Risk Control (HIRARC) method. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed, involving observations, interviews, documentation reviews, and a literature study with 15 respondents. The results indicate that the dominant hazards were falls from heights (100%) with a risk score of 25 (extreme), being struck by falling materials (93.33%) with a score of 16 (high), slips/trips (86.67%) with a score of 12 (high), cuts/lacerations (80%) with a score of 6 (moderate), and electric shock (73.33%) with a score of 12 (high). Implemented controls included the use of Personal Protective Equipment (100%), safety briefings (93.33%), standard-compliant scaffolding (86.67%), safety officer supervision (86.67%), and OHS signage (80%). Workers' perceptions yielded an average score of 4.21 ("agree"), indicating that OHS risk management implementation has been effective. However, improvements in training, supervision of work at heights, and fall protection systems are still required to minimize workplace accidents..

items.title: Analisa Risiko Kesehatan Dan Keselamatan Kerja (K3) Dengan Metode Jsa (Job Safety Analysis) Pada Proyek Pembangunan Sdn Ii Sibon Kec.Pasrepan
items.abstract: This study aims to identify potential hazards, risk levels, and Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) control measures for the SDN II Sibon construction project in Pasrepan District. The study employs the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) method using a descriptive-qualitative approach, involving observations, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires administered to 16 workers. Risk assessment is conducted based on likelihood and severity parameters. The results indicate that workers' OHS knowledge ranges from reasonably good to high (62.5%–87.5%); however, the implementation of OHS measures is not yet optimal. The highest risks identified include heat exhaustion (81.25%), slipping (75%), and muscle pain (75%). Based on the JSA, three hazards were classified as extreme (scoring 20): soil collapse/stockpile collapse, excavation collapse, and falls from heights. Risk control measures implemented include engineering controls, administrative controls, and the use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)—specifically scaffolding and guardrails, shoring, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), toolbox meetings, OHS inspections, work permits, and task-specific PPE. Consistent implementation of these controls is expected to minimize accident risks and foster a safe, productive work environment.

items.title: Analisis Beban Kerja Instruktur Pelatihan Keselamatan Kerja Pertambangan Menggunakan Metode FTE
items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a fundamental pillar in the high-risk mining industry. Ensuring worker competence through mandatory safety training is a regulatory obligation under the Mining Safety Management System (SMKP). However, fluctuations in the number of training participants often lead to an imbalance in the workload of trainers, which can potentially reduce the quality of safety education. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of Training Need Analysis (TNA) and quantify the ideal requirement for safety trainers at PT Freeport Indonesia. The research design is descriptive quantitative. The research population includes all safety training programs under the Mining Safety Division. The sample taken consists of 21 mandatory training types within the Technical Support Division, with a total workload target of 10,872 training hours. The research variables include total training hours, classroom capacity, training frequency, and the effective working time of the trainers. Data collection was conducted through field observations and the recapitulation of the company's secondary ONA data. Data analysis utilizes mathematical calculations of the Full Time Equivalent (FTE) index. The results show that the mechanism for implementing TNA and training has normatively run systematically. However, the quantitative workload analysis reveals that the trainer's FTE index reaches 15.64. This figure indicates a significant workload excess (overload) within the safety training unit. It can be concluded that to complete the mandatory training targets within an optimal and safe six-month timeframe, a minimum availability of 16 trainers dedicated to the division is required.

items.abstract: The fishery processing and export industry is a key sector that contributes to the national economy, but it poses high occupational safety and health (OSH) risks due to the use of sharp equipment, manual handling of materials, exposure to low temperatures and chemicals, and forklift traffic. This study aims to identify hazards, assess risk levels, and develop control recommendations using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Risk Control (HIRARC) method based on the AS/NZS 4360:2004 standard and the Hierarchy of Control principle. The study employed a descriptive observational approach with a case study design in the fisheries processing and export industry in Indonesia. Data were collected through field observations and workplace safety inspections, then analyzed based on the likelihood and severity of risks. The study identified 23 potential hazards, consisting of 10 health hazards and 13 safety hazards. In the health hazard category, eight high-risk and two moderate-risk hazards were identified, while in the safety hazard category, there was one extreme-risk, seven high-risk, and five moderate-risk hazards. The highest risk stemmed from the intersection of forklift lanes with pedestrian walkways, which has the potential to cause fatal accidents. In addition, non-compliance issues were identified, such as expired fire extinguishers, the absence of safety signs at intersections, obstructed access to fire extinguishers, and inadequate ergonomic working conditions. The HIRARC method has proven effective in prioritizing risks as the basis for developing control measures. Control measures should prioritize extreme and high risks through engineering controls, administrative controls, routine inspections, and strengthening the occupational safety and health (OSH) culture to create a safer, healthier, and more productive work environment.

items.abstract: Construction projects are dynamic fields fraught with various risks that can affect productivity, performance, quality, and the project budget. This research aims to analyze the risks that emerged in the Mega Grup Indonesia Islamic School Ciamis Building Construction Project and determine appropriate handling strategies using the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method. This research employs a quantitative approach with data collection techniques through field observation, interviews, and questionnaires involving 16 respondents directly involved in the project. The collected data were analyzed by calculating the severity, occurrence, and detection values for each identified risk. These values were then multiplied to obtain the risk priority number to determine risk handling priorities. The research results identified 17 potential risks. Three risks were categorized as high level: the influence of the rainy season and bad weather with an risk priority number of 74.4, work delays with an risk priority number of 61.8, and flooding with an risk priority number of 58. One risk fell into the medium category, namely workers' non-compliance with occupational health and safety regulations with an risk priority number of 40.2, and the other 13 risks were classified as low. As mitigation steps, material relocation can be implemented to address the influence of the rainy season and bad weather, adding labor to overcome work delays, cleaning drainage channels and utilizing water for flood risk, and providing personal protective equipment facilities and strict supervision to improve compliance with health and safety regulations for the risk of workers non-compliance with occupational health and safety rules.

items.title: ANALYSIS OF FACTORS AFFECTING THE OPERATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS OF AIRCRAFT CONTROL SYSTEMS
items.abstract: The article highlights the mismatch between existing design approaches and the conditions of modern combat operations, as reliability assessment is often conducted only for individual factors in isolation. Based on the system analysis, the authors identified and classified three main groups of influencing factors: natural (meteorological conditions, geophysical factors, and physical effects), anthropogenic (combat conditions, man-made interference, and the human factor), and technical (hardware, information-processing and algorithmic, and dynamic factors). Their components and the nature of each factor’s impact on the aircraft control system are described in detail. Based on the results of the analysis, three detailed structural-hierarchical diagrams of the influencing factors have been developed. The generalized structural-hierarchical framework allows for a comprehensive consideration of internal and external threats that arise throughout the entire aircraft lifecycle and directly affect combat employment effectiveness. The authors substantiate that the reliability and operational effectiveness of an aircraft control system must be considered as equivalent and interrelated characteristics. The created structural-hierarchical framework will serve as a foundation for the subsequent determination of the minimum necessary set of properties that modern and prospective aircraft control systems must possess.

items.title: Anchor-ECC: Local Integrity Checking for Watermarked LLM Outputs via Error-Correcting Codes
items.abstract: LLM watermarking has become an effective approach to distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text by embedding detectable patterns during generation. However, a small post-generation edit may change the meaning of the text without removing its overall watermark signal, creating a risk that the modified content is still attributed to the original model. We propose Anchor-ECC, which incorporates the error-correcting code (ECC) constraints and explicit boundary anchors into the watermark structure and pairs them with a dynamic-programming decoder to detect and localize post-generation edits. Across Qwen3-8B, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and OPT-125M, the approximate-hard setting achieves about 99.7% block-level true positive rate (TPR) with at most 7.6% false alarm rate (FAR) for edit detection under mixed insertions, deletions, and substitutions, while preserving the distinction between watermarked outputs and unwatermarked text. Additional quality experiments identify lower-perplexity configurations that retain strong edit-detection performance. Together, these results extend LLM watermarking from source identification to local integrity verification while supporting configurable trade-offs between detection reliability and generation quality.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnostic Medical Imaging and Radiotherapy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare, particularly in diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of diagnostic medical imaging and radiotherapy has witnessed significant advancements, revolutionizing the healthcare landscape. This review delves into its diverse applications, exploring its potential to boost accuracy, streamline workflows, and improve patient outcomes. A systematic literature search identified relevant studies on AI's role in these domains. Articles covered topics like image analysis, pattern recognition, decision support, and treatment planning. AI algorithms, performance, and integration into clinical practice were critically evaluated. In diagnostic imaging, AI shines in modalities like MRI, CT, and PET. AI algorithms excel in image interpretation, aiding early detection, characterization, and staging of various diseases. Additionally, these tools show promise in predicting treatment response and personalizing treatment plans. Within radiotherapy, AI automates and improves treatment steps. Machine learning algorithms efficiently contour target volumes and organs at risk, facilitating optimal treatment planning. Real-time image guidance and AI-driven adaptive radiotherapy techniques enhance precision and safety during treatment delivery. Moreover, AI-based predictive models assist in assessing outcomes and optimizing therapeutic strategies, ultimately improving patient care. Despite the advancements, challenges like data privacy, standardization, and ethical considerations persist. This review paints a comprehensive picture of AI's current applications in diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy, highlighting its transformative impact on disease diagnosis and treatment planning. As AI evolves, its integration into clinical practice holds immense potential to revolutionize patient care, ushering in a new era of precision medicine.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Teaching and Learning: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing mathematics education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated feedback, assessment support, and teacher assistance. AI-enabled systems can adapt tasks to learners’ needs, provide immediate feedback, generate practice questions, and help identify misconceptions. Recent reviews suggest that adaptive platforms, intelligent tutoring systems, and generative-AI tools can support engagement, self-paced learning, conceptual understanding, and mathematical problem-solving when used under effective teacher guidance.link.springer+1 However, AI is not a replacement for mathematics teachers. Concerns remain about inaccurate AI-generated solutions, student overdependence, privacy risks, unequal access to devices and internet connectivity, algorithmic bias, and limited teacher preparedness. Evidence also remains mixed, particularly because many studies are short-term and report limited standardized measures of learning impact. This paper reviews the opportunities and challenges of AI in mathematics teaching and learning and proposes a Human–AI Collaborative Framework for responsible, equitable, and pedagogically meaningful implementation.frontiersin+1

items.title: Application of Large Language Models and Natural Language Generation in Content Creation: A Retrieval-Augmented and Preference-Aligned Framework
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have substantially advanced natural language generation (NLG), but high-quality content creation remains constrained by hallucination, limited controllability, retrieval noise, domain shift, and computational cost. This study proposes Retrieval-Augmented and Preference-Aligned Generation (RAP-Gen), a unified framework that integrates retrieval-augmented generation, factual preference alignment, in-context learning, and denoising pre-training. The framework combines a dense semantic retriever with an encoder–decoder generator, introduces pairwise factual-preference supervision for controllable generation, aligns retrieval and generation distributions, and uses structured text corruption to improve robustness to incomplete or noisy inputs. Experiments are reported on summarization, long-form creative writing, and knowledge-intensive question answering using CNN/DailyMail, WritingPrompts, Natural Questions, and general language-modeling data. The reported results show that RAP-Gen improves ROUGE, BERTScore, perplexity, FactScore, and human-rated factuality relative to the baselines listed in the manuscript. Ablation results indicate that removing retrieval, preference alignment, or denoising degrades performance, supporting the complementary roles of external knowledge, preference signals, and robust pre-training. Additional analyses examine the number of retrieved documents, attention over retrieved evidence, robustness under input perturbation, model scaling, and in-context learning. Because the supplied material does not include raw predictions, code, repeated-run variance, annotator agreement statistics, or complete benchmark configurations, the numerical results are interpreted as reported experimental outcomes rather than independently reproducible evidence. The study contributes an integrated design for knowledge-grounded, preference-aware content generation and identifies evaluation and reproducibility requirements for future work.

items.title: Application of the ELMERI Observation Method for Occupational Health and Safety Performance Assessment in a Manufacturing Plant
items.abstract: Manufacturing workplaces involve hazards associated with machinery, material handling, worker practices, and environmental conditions. This study aimed to assess occupational health and safety conditions and identify priorities for improvement at a water fixture component manufacturing facility in Istanbul, Türkiye. A descriptive assessment was conducted using the ELMERI Observation Method across seven categories. A single researcher conducted observations three days per week from April to June 2021 and recorded 114 checklist-item ratings, comprising 74 correct and 40 incorrect classifications. Category-specific and overall safety indices were calculated from these counts. The overall index was 64.9%. Safety-related behavior had the highest category index (83.3%), followed by first aid and fire safety (71.4%), order and cleanliness (68.4%), and machine safety (66.7%). Lower indices were obtained for ergonomics (50.0%), industrial hygiene (44.4%), and floors and passageways (25.0%). The findings indicate that favorable ratings for observed worker practices coexisted with deficiencies in physical workplace conditions. Priorities included unobstructed passageways, machine guarding, ventilation, and ergonomic improvements. Unequal observation counts, potential observer bias, and the single-facility design limit interpretation and generalizability. The assessment identified practical priorities for the facility; the effectiveness of the proposed corrective actions requires follow-up evaluation.

items.title: Approach for Dual Probabilistic Linguistic Decision-Making Under Unknown Attribute Weights Based on Archimedean Power Muirhead Mean Operators
items.abstract: Dual probabilistic linguistic term sets (DPLTSs) provide a powerful tool for describing uncertain, hesitant, and bipolar linguistic assessments in complex decision-making settings. Current aggregation methods for dual probabilistic linguistic information still have drawbacks. They can hardly mitigate the interference brought by biased assessment values and fail to capture the correlations among arbitrary attributes. To address these limitations, this paper develops a new class of dual probabilistic linguistic Archimedean power Muirhead mean (DPLAPMM) operators for multipleattribute decision making (MADM). First, by combining the advantages of Archimedean triangular norms with the power Muirhead mean (PMM) operator, the DPLAPMM operator together with its weighted form are developed. The proposed operators can reduce the impact of unreasonable evaluation values while modeling the interrelationships among any number of attributes. Then, a dual probabilistic linguistic entropy is constructed to obtain objective attribute weights, which are combined with subjective weights to generate comprehensive attribute weights. Based on these results, a MADM method is established under a dual probabilistic linguistic environment. An illustrative case concerning industrial artificial intelligence (AI) project selection is used to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method, and comparative analyses show its flexibility and effectiveness over existing approaches.
